title: Gemini: Mapping and Architecture Co-exploration for Large-scale DNN Chiplet Accelerators
problem: Chiplet technology for DNN accelerators introduces expensive packaging costs and costly Die-to-Die interfaces that consume more area and power while offering lower bandwidth than onchip interconnects. The key challenge is jointly optimizing both architecture and DNN layer mapping across chiplets to minimize costs while maximizing performance and energy efficiency.
motivation: Chiplet technology enables integration of more transistors with higher yield in the post-Moore era to meet the increasing computational demands of AI applications.
method: Gemini uses a layer-centric encoding (representing each neural network layer's position across chiplets individually, rather than encoding the entire system at once) to describe spatial layer mappings. It optimizes two aspects together: the physical hardware architecture and the assignment of DNN layers to that architecture, instead of designing hardware first and then mapping layers afterwards. A configurable template evaluates each candidate design by measuring manufacturing cost, inference performance, and energy consumption.
key_novelty: Layer-centric encoding (describing each DNN layer's position across chiplets individually) enables optimizing hardware architecture and layer mapping at the same time, instead of optimizing them separately.
contributions: Layer-centric encoding method for representing spatial mappings across chiplet boundaries
Gemini co-exploration framework that jointly optimizes architecture and DNN layer mapping
Analysis of untapped optimization opportunities specific to chiplet scenarios
Achieves 1.98x performance and 1.41x energy efficiency improvements over SOTA with only 14.3% cost increase
